focus: 1952 presidential-election enforcement chain: identify police chief Yun, separate complainants/investigators/administrative superiors, and sharpen the August 12 investigation-halt lead

documents_opened.type: contemporary Dong-A Ilbo reproduced by National Institute of Korean History
documents_opened.finding: Full text says Liberal Party Central Election Countermeasures Committee figures filed an August 4 complaint against Prime Minister Chang Taek-sang, Home Minister Kim Tae-son and 'Yun, Director of the Public Security Bureau' for alleged presidential/vice-presidential election-law and civil-service-law violations. Prosecutor General Han Kyok-man said investigation would begin and Supreme Prosecutors' Office prosecutor Yi Chong-u would handle it. The report names committee chairman Chae Kyu-hang and associates including U Mun, Yang U-jong, Yu Hwa-chong and Shin Tae-chol, with some inconsistency between the prose lists that should be preserved rather than silently harmonized.

documents_opened.type: official National Archives of Korea institutional history
documents_opened.finding: Official institutional chronology lists Yun U-gyong (윤우경) as Home Ministry Public Security Bureau director from 1952-05-25 to 1952-09-16. This independently identifies the complaint's otherwise surname-only 'Yun 치안국장' as 윤우경 for the August 1952 date.

documents_opened.type: authoritative biographical reference / Academy of Korean Studies
documents_opened.finding: Biographical entry gives 윤우경 (尹宇景), 1900-1995, and confirms his 1952 Home Ministry Public Security Bureau directorship. It also records a June 1952 order through the bureau's surveillance section to monitor National Assembly members, making him an independently significant police-administration node rather than a surname-only subordinate.

documents_opened.type: National Institute of Korean History day index
documents_opened.finding: The August 12 index explicitly titles an item '金泰善 내무장관, 선거사범 일체 수사 중지를 지시'. The index establishes existence/date/topic but not yet recipient, legal basis, exceptions or implementation.

documents_opened.type: National Institute of Korean History day index
documents_opened.finding: Index separately records Kim Tae-son convening provincial governors and police chiefs ahead of the presidential/vice-presidential election, candidate-registration closure, statements by Yim Young-shin/Yi Gap-song/Chon Chin-han, lifting of emergency martial law, and Ko Chae-bong's designation as Seoul mayor. This reinforces the need to separate election administration from post-election criminal investigation.

documents_opened.type: authoritative biographical reference / Academy of Korean Studies
documents_opened.finding: Entry gives 김태선 (金泰善), 1903-05-18 to 1977-01-07; confirms prior Public Security Bureau/Seoul police leadership, appointment as Home Minister in July 1952 and removal about a month later. This anchors the minister node and warns against conflating him with the contemporary Public Security Bureau director 윤우경.

documents_opened.type: official Supreme Prosecutors' Office institutional history
documents_opened.finding: Official prosecution history confirms Han Kyok-man became the fourth Prosecutor General on 1952-03-14 and was in office during the August complaint/investigation episode.

documents_opened.type: contemporary Chosun Ilbo reproduced by National Institute of Korean History
documents_opened.finding: Earlier May 10 item records Prosecutor General Han Kyok-man publicly explaining prosecution in the Seo Min-ho case, useful as independent confirmation of his prosecutorial office and public-facing role before the August election complaint.

documents_opened.type: National Institute of Korean History academic publication
documents_opened.finding: Study reproduces the 1952 Liberal Party central officer roster, including Yang U-jong as political-affairs director and Yu Hwa-chong as general-affairs director. This independently anchors two complainant-side actors named in the August 6 report.
Rechecked candidate-introduction attachment indexing Yim Young-shin. Retained as a boundary check: candidate identity and enforcement attribution are distinct evidence questions.

verified_findings.claim: The surname-only '윤치안국장' accused in the August 4/6 Liberal Party election-law complaint can be identified as 윤우경 (尹宇景), because the National Archives institutional chronology places Yun U-gyong in the Home Ministry Public Security Bureau director post continuously from 1952-05-25 through 1952-09-16.

The August complaint chain contains at least four actor layers that must not be collapsed: Liberal Party complainants, accused executive/police officials, Prosecutor General Han Kyok-man as the official announcing investigation, and prosecutor Yi Chong-u as the reported case investigator.

Kim Tae-son and Yun U-gyong were different officials in August 1952: Kim was Home Minister, while Yun was Public Security Bureau director. Earlier data should not use a generic 'police chief Yun' once this officeholder identity is available.

The August 12 source presently verifies an instruction by Home Minister Kim Tae-son to halt investigation of election offenders only at title/index level; recipient, statutory authority, scope and actual compliance remain unverified and must stay OPEN.

The August 6 complaint report itself contains a minor name-list inconsistency among complainant-side signatories/participants. The graph should preserve this provenance conflict until the original complaint is recovered rather than manufacture a single clean list.
